origin.description: Valid completions after the ``$`` extractor are generated by ``.DollarNames``. For a list it matches ``pattern`` against ``names(x)`` via ``findMatches``; for an environment it uses ``ls`` or ``findMatches`` depending on the ``fuzzy`` completion setting; the default method returns an empty character vector for atomic objects and otherwise matches ``names(x)``.

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: The object after ``$`` in the partial command line.

origin.details: Completion after ``$`` and ``@`` is controlled by the ``ops`` setting in ``rc.settings``. The environment method uses ``ls(x, all.names = TRUE, pattern = pattern)`` when ``fuzzy`` is false.
origin.value: A character vector of matching names.
origin.example:
library(utils)
e <- new.env()
e$foo <- 1
assign("bar", 2, e)
assign(".hidden", 3, e)
paste(sort(.DollarNames(e, "")), collapse = ",")

translation.description: Valid completions after ``$`` for a dict (named list), ``REnvironment``, or other object with a ``names`` sequence; atomic scalars yield an empty list.

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: Object after ``$``; ``dict`` and ``REnvironment`` dispatch like R list and environment methods.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.description: Partial name, matched as a regular expression like R ``grep`` / ``findMatches``.

translation.details: Reuses the same default completion settings and ``findMatches`` port as ``AtNames``.
translation.example:
from utils.dollar_names import DollarNames, REnvironment
env = REnvironment(foo=1, bar=2, _hidden={".hidden": 3})
print(",".join(sorted(DollarNames(env, ""))))
